# Python-semantics traps in Rust ports

Every one of these produced a confirmed parity defect during the v14 P2 ports (found by codex finder passes with reproduced counterexamples). Check each when porting or reviewing.

1. **str whitespace sets differ.** Python `str.strip()`/`split()`/`isspace()` treat `\x1c`–`\x1f` (FS/GS/RS/US), `\x85`, and more as whitespace; Rust `trim()`/`split_whitespace()` (Unicode White_Space) do not. Bit activity twice and buckets once. Use core `pystr.rs` — never raw `trim()`/`split_whitespace()` where Python parity matters. (`str.splitlines()` has its own, larger boundary set — render mirrors it.)
2. **Duplicate JSON object keys.** Python `json.loads`/orjson keep the LAST occurrence (by decoded key); sonic-rs preserves duplicates and field lookup returns the FIRST. FIXED AT THE ROOT (commit 25753d8): parse.rs normalizes persisted payload Values last-wins at parse (tool input, Other raws, mcp_meta, response, blocking_error, structured_output, permission_denials); `tool_use_result` normalizes at its typed gateway `parse_tool_result` (perf: biggest payload class); `normalize_last_wins` is pub for non-parse entry points (cost usage JSON). Readers that bypass the gateway on raw results keep local last-wins (render's result-side serialization).
3. **Float formatting: THREE distinct layouts.** (a) Rust `format!("{:e}")`/`{}`/plain Ryū are NOT tie-exact vs Python/ES shortest digits (698957826421429.2) — use `ryu-js` for digits. (b) ES layout ≠ Python `str(float)` layout: ES `1e-7`, Python `1e-07`; canonical_json needs ES, render/repr needs Python layout over ryu-js digits (orjson matches Python EXCEPT no exponent zero-padding). (c) Python `round()` is half-even. Fuzz new formatting paths against Python.
4. **Value preservation over type-filtering.** Python stores whatever the JSON carried; mirror the exact Python op (`str(7)`="7" coercions included). orjson parses `-0` (int) to `0`.
5. **Materialization drops.** The Python parse path drops events whose timestamps can't materialize; Rust paths consuming parse_bytes directly must apply the same drops. (P3 moves the guard to parse time.)
6. **Code-point vs byte string ops.** Python slicing/truncation is code-point-based.
7. **Big integers.** Python ints are arbitrary precision; Python `/` on ints is exact true division — mirror the op order (bit cost). Project big ints via int-from-string (digest doc 35f43592).
8. **Regex engine dialect ≠ pattern bytes.** `\s`/`\w`/`\b` differ (controls, combining marks, İ). See d458ca8; expand divergent classes explicitly or document-and-pin per the established convention.
9. **Timestamp precision.** Python datetime is µs; chrono keeps ns, changing near-tie sort order. Truncate to µs at core parse_timestamp (smallmods lane).
10. **Lenient shape fallbacks.** Python `.get()` chains fall back silently; Rust `require_*` rejects. Mirror the exact access pattern per field.
11. **`interrupted` is marker OR interruptedMessageId** (parser.py:405). Diff ported predicates against the MATERIALIZER's semantics (py/event.rs), not just the same-named core method.
12. **sonic-rs mutable object API is HASH-ordered with a RANDOMIZED seed.** `as_object_mut()` / `Object::new()+insert()` do NOT preserve insertion order and are non-deterministic per run — a dedup built on them silently scrambled tool-input key order and broke render parity intermittently. NEVER mutate a sonic Value through the mutable API where order matters: rebuild dup-carrying subtrees via re-serialize (`write_deduped`) + `from_str`, which preserves order.
